posts.text:
For the GPT-Live-1's intelligence, Tau3 tests whether a voice agent can actually complete customer-support tasks across airline, retail, and telecom scenarios.

Paired with GPT-6 Astra at medium reasoning effort, GPT-Live-1 completed 83.6% of tasks on the first attempt, compared with 45.7% for GPT-Realtime-2.1.

The same pairing scored 38.1% on TauBanking, where agents need to find information in banking documents and apply it while using tools to resolve customer requests.

Of course, people chatting with our builds don’t talk in perfectly timed turns.

They pause to think, interrupt with another question, or say “mm-hmm” without expecting you to stop:
• GPT-Live-1 scored 97.3% on Artificial Analysis’s Conversational Dynamics benchmark, which evaluates when to wait, take a turn, respond to an interruption, or keep speaking through a short acknowledgment.
• On Full Duplex Bench v1.5, it scored 80.1% on interactivity across overlapping speech, background voices, side conversations, and interruptions.
• In Full Duplex Bench v1, it began responding 0.798 seconds after the user’s turn ended, compared with 1.41 seconds for GPT-Realtime-2.1. That measures the wait before the reply starts, not how quickly the model speaks.

Getting the task right also means following a request when someone pauses, hesitates, or corrects themselves.

With a backend model handling tool calls, the GPT-Live-1 setup achieved these results on Full Duplex Bench v3:
• 87% tool-calling success for completing the correct sequence of tool calls.
• 90% on the separate response-quality evaluation.

Read more in the launch blog:

posts.text:
如果每天真实发生的 Agent 调用，都能反过来告诉模型「下一轮该学什么」呢？

NeoHorse-1 尝试把这件事做成一个持续训练闭环。

系统里的 Routing Harness 会根据任务难度选择模型，同时记录执行轨迹、工具调用和结果。

这些真实交互会被整理成训练数据。系统先判断哪些轨迹有效、哪里失败，再把任务按能力需求组织成课程，用来更新模型。

训练后的模型重新回到 Harness 里跑新任务，继续暴露新的能力缺口。

于是形成了一条很自然的循环：

执行任务 → 找到短板 → 组织数据 → 更新模型 → 再回到真实任务。

实验覆盖 10 个 benchmark。4B 模型平均分从 58.94 提升到 64.87，9B 从 65.60 提升到 69.04。

更值得注意的是，同样训练配置下，Routing Harness 收集的真实交互轨迹，比公开合成 Agent 数据平均高 6.26 个百分点。

现在 Harness 可能会逐渐从执行层走进训练层。

Agent 每天怎么被使用、在哪里失败，本身就可能成为下一版模型最有价值的数据来源。

posts.text:
As a follow-up, it's exceedingly unlikely that training on user data contributes much to frontier model gains in areas like math -- those come from scaling up pretraining and RLVR. User data is more likely used to find failure modes or situations that are hard to recreate with hired annotators.

That said, model companies vary in how aggressively they train on user data (and uploading repos isn't hypothetical). I wish there were stronger norms around disclosing how companies train on user data -- with what methods, and to improve what capabilities.

quotedTweet.text:
This isn't the most notable aspect of today's news, but on the user data issue, there are different kinds of *training on user data* with very different privacy/IP implications. Sadly, AI cos don't like to disclose what they're doing.

- pretrain on user data, with users' tokens as prediction targets: high regurgitation risk, improper
- use user prompts to distill large models into small ones: low regurg. risk, some companies probably do this
- use user traces to construct RL tasks: low regurg. risk, because RL has low memorization abilities, but can extract customer IP, depending on how it's done. Ranges from benign "use explicit user feedback in reward model training" to invasive "upload user's coding environment and commit history to turn into rl envs"

"De-identification" is weak -- you can identify someone with a small number of bits, and long traces have more than enough. And it doesn't affect IP leakage concerns.
quotedTweet.translationZh:
这不是今天新闻中最值得关注的方面，但在用户数据问题上，*用用户数据训练*有不同类型，对隐私/IP 的影响也非常不同。遗憾的是，AI 公司并不喜欢披露自己在做什么。

- 用用户数据做预训练，把用户的 token 作为预测目标：复述风险高，不合适
- 用用户提示词把大模型蒸馏成小模型：复述风险低，一些公司很可能在这么做
- 用用户轨迹构建 RL 任务：复述风险低，因为 RL 的记忆能力较弱，但可能提取客户 IP，取决于具体做法。范围从良性的“在奖励模型训练中使用明确的用户反馈”，到侵入性的“上传用户的编码环境和提交历史，用来转化成 rl envs”

“去标识化”很弱——只需少量比特就能识别出一个人，而长轨迹包含的信息绰绰有余。而且它也无法消除 IP 泄露方面的担忧。

expert.why: RLHF、后训练、推理和 Alignment

posts.translationZh:
补充一点：用用户数据训练几乎不太可能显著推动前沿模型在数学等领域的提升，这些提升来自扩大预训练规模和 RLVR。用户数据更可能用于发现故障模式，或发现难以用雇佣标注员复现的情境。

"Symbolic learning" is simply "machine learning" (automatically learn function x -> y given examples of (x, y) pairs), but where the substrate is symbolic, i.e. the functions you learn are code-like, not curve-like.

The term is in opposition to "parametric learning" or "curve-fitting".

Symbolic learning does not mean that the system avoids numbers or probabilities. It means its learned representation are discrete, explicit, parsimonious, code-like.

quotedTweet.text:
Yesterday, Microsoft's monthly Patch Tuesday had fixes for 974 security vulnerabilities, almost all of them found by AI systems. That's a ridiculously large number, a new record by far in fact.

Does this mean we're seeing some sort of AI security apocalypse? No, quite the opposite. It means that we're finally clearing out the vast number of security holes that have been lurking all this time in our software.

The Doomer view is that this will continue without end, and that if you keep getting smarter AI systems they will *always* find new bugs. That's simply untrue; it implies that all software has an *infinite* number of security holes, but a program with a finite number of lines of code simply cannot have an infinite number of vulnerabilities. What we actually have is a large but limited pool of problems, and the AI systems are rapidly finding them.

Eventually, and eventually isn't that far off, the well is going to start drying up. It will get harder and harder to find new security holes. Over the next few years, we will also start doing formal verification of software, that is, mathematically proving that the software lacks bugs of certain sorts. (AIs turn out to be very good at formally proving things.)

So, what's happening is *good*. We are rapidly finding bugs that have been lurking for years and sometimes decades, and we're removing them, and newly built software will get AI examination and will be much less likely to have security vulnerabilities in the first place. The situation is getting better, not worse, and it's getting better rapidly.

We have been in a continuous computer security crisis since the Morris Worm in 1988. We are finally starting to climb out of it, thanks to AI. This is not a tragedy at all.

这是否意味着我们正在看到某种 AI 安全末日？不是，恰恰相反。这意味着我们终于在清理那些一直潜伏在软件中的大量安全漏洞。

reviewedPosts.text:
如果每天真实发生的 Agent 调用，都能反过来告诉模型「下一轮该学什么」呢？

NeoHorse-1 尝试把这件事做成一个持续训练闭环。

系统里的 Routing Harness 会根据任务难度选择模型，同时记录执行轨迹、工具调用和结果。

这些真实交互会被整理成训练数据。系统先判断哪些轨迹有效、哪里失败，再把任务按能力需求组织成课程，用来更新模型。

训练后的模型重新回到 Harness 里跑新任务，继续暴露新的能力缺口。

于是形成了一条很自然的循环：

执行任务 → 找到短板 → 组织数据 → 更新模型 → 再回到真实任务。

实验覆盖 10 个 benchmark。4B 模型平均分从 58.94 提升到 64.87，9B 从 65.60 提升到 69.04。

更值得注意的是，同样训练配置下，Routing Harness 收集的真实交互轨迹，比公开合成 Agent 数据平均高 6.26 个百分点。

现在 Harness 可能会逐渐从执行层走进训练层。

Agent 每天怎么被使用、在哪里失败，本身就可能成为下一版模型最有价值的数据来源。

看到一个特别适合内容创作者的概念——Shallow Intent「浅层意图」。

很多 AI 内容让人不舒服，可能并不是因为一眼就能看出「这是 AI 写的」，而是它看起来很精致、信息很多，但你仔细往下挖，会发现每个细节背后并没有多少真正的思考。

作者举了一个很好的例子。一张 AI 海报第一眼非常漂亮，但人物年代错了、物体关系不合理，甚至连画面的核心寓意都表达反了。

AI 很容易把「看起来投入了很多心思」这件事做得很便宜。

这对写东西其实也一样。

那些真正值得保留的，是那些 AI 最难替你决定的东西，例如为什么写这一段、为什么选这个例子、什么该删、你到底观察到了什么，以及你希望读者看完以后留下什么。

我现在觉得，AI 时代做内容，一个很重要的能力可能就是提高自己的 Intent Density「意图密度」。

AI 可以帮你把东西做出来，但最后那层「为什么这样做」，还是得自己放进去。

很推荐这篇。

If you ask a coding agent to write a program that maps x to y given some (x, y) examples, you're doing a very expensive form of symbolic learning. In fact what you're doing is specifically a form of DL-guided program synthesis (that's what LLM codegen is).

However there are far more efficient (data-wise and compute wise) ways to do symbolic learning. By many orders of magnitude.

reviewedPosts.author: fchollet
reviewedPosts.text:
Symbolic learning, correctly implemented, is in every way parallel to deep learning and comparable to it 1:1, but with a different representation substrate, and accordingly with a different learning mechanism.

The goals are the same, the general principles are the same. The representations differ. But they may end up converging eventually.
reviewedPosts.evidence: 符号学习表示基底不同

reviewedPosts.author: fchollet
reviewedPosts.text:
Symbolic learning also does not mean "writing the representations by hand" (you are thinking of "symbolic AI" from the 1970s-1990s). Nowadays when you write by hand a function x -> y given examples of (x, y) pairs, we just call that "programming."

Symbolic learning is emphatically a form of machine learning: the representations are automatically derived from data, just like with deep learning.

reviewedPosts.author: fchollet
reviewedPosts.text:
"Symbolic learning" is simply "machine learning" (automatically learn function x -> y given examples of (x, y) pairs), but where the substrate is symbolic, i.e. the functions you learn are code-like, not curve-like.

The term is in opposition to "parametric learning" or "curve-fitting".

Symbolic learning does not mean that the system avoids numbers or probabilities. It means its learned representation are discrete, explicit, parsimonious, code-like.

For the GPT-Live-1's intelligence, Tau3 tests whether a voice agent can actually complete customer-support tasks across airline, retail, and telecom scenarios.

Paired with GPT-6 Astra at medium reasoning effort, GPT-Live-1 completed 83.6% of tasks on the first attempt, compared with 45.7% for GPT-Realtime-2.1.

The same pairing scored 38.1% on TauBanking, where agents need to find information in banking documents and apply it while using tools to resolve customer requests.

Of course, people chatting with our builds don’t talk in perfectly timed turns.

They pause to think, interrupt with another question, or say “mm-hmm” without expecting you to stop:
• GPT-Live-1 scored 97.3% on Artificial Analysis’s Conversational Dynamics benchmark, which evaluates when to wait, take a turn, respond to an interruption, or keep speaking through a short acknowledgment.
• On Full Duplex Bench v1.5, it scored 80.1% on interactivity across overlapping speech, background voices, side conversations, and interruptions.
• In Full Duplex Bench v1, it began responding 0.798 seconds after the user’s turn ended, compared with 1.41 seconds for GPT-Realtime-2.1. That measures the wait before the reply starts, not how quickly the model speaks.

Getting the task right also means following a request when someone pauses, hesitates, or corrects themselves.

With a backend model handling tool calls, the GPT-Live-1 setup achieved these results on Full Duplex Bench v3:
• 87% tool-calling success for completing the correct sequence of tool calls.
• 90% on the separate response-quality evaluation.
